title: A Protocol for Decellularizing Mouse Cochleae for Inner Ear Tissue Engineering
protocol: Decapitate an appropriately euthanized, 15-week-old mouse by cutting between the skull and first cervical vertebra with a sharp pair of surgical scissors.
Spray down the head with 70% ethanol to disinfect.
Bisect the skull in a mid-sagittal plane using the same sharp pair of surgical scissors.
Remove the brain tissue from the skull using a pair of forceps.
Identify the temporal bone through the presence of the auditory and vestibular nerve roots on the interior of the skull.
Carefully cut through the skull to isolate the temporal bone from the remainder of the skull.
Insert fine forceps into the opening of the ear canal approximately 5 mm deep.
Gently break open the bone of the bulla to cause it to fracture.
Pry away the remainder of the bulla from the temporal bone to expose the bony labyrinth of the cochlea.
Place a Petri dish large enough to hold the temporal bone underneath the dissecting scope field of view.
Fill the Petri dish with Phosphate Buffered Saline (PBS) to cover the temporal bone.
Submerge the temporal bone with the bulla removed in PBS, ensuring the oval and round windows face up.
Remove the stapedial artery using an ultra-fine pair of forceps.
Insert one tip of the ultra-fine forceps through the arch of the stapes where the artery passed through.
Lift the stapes upward to disarticulate it from the oval window.
Using one tip of the ultra-fine forceps, puncture the oval and round windows.
Mix 1x PBS with antibiotic-antimycotic and penicillin-streptomycin to prepare a solution for perfusion.
Position tubing over the oval window of the cochlea using ultra-fine forceps.
Perfuse 2 mL of prepared solution through the cochlea over 5 minutes carefully by hand or using a perfusion pump.
Stabilize the vestibular portion of the temporal bone with fine, self-closing forceps during perfusion if manually perfusing.
Remove and discard any remaining muscle tissue and bone fragments using fine forceps.
If necessary, store isolated cochleae at 4 °C in 10% anti-anti and 10% pen-strep solution in PBS for up to seven days with regular changes of antibiotic solution every 48 h.
Fill a 20-mL glass scintillation vial with a 1% sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) solution in de-ionized (DI) water.
Cut the tip off of a plastic 7-mL transfer pipette using a razor blade so that the opening is large enough for a cochlea to pass through.
Gently draw the cochlea up into the transfer pipette and expel it into the 1% SDS solution-filled scintillation vial.
Circulate 2 mL of 1% SDS in DI water through the cochlea using a transfer pipette.
Place the scintillation vial containing the cochlea into a rotator, set to rotate at 10 rpm for 72 h at room temperature.
Change 1% SDS solution every 24 h over a 72 h period.
Wash the cochlea three times for 30 min each with DI water.
Remove remaining DI water from the scintillation vial, leaving just enough to keep the cochlea submerged.
Add 5 mL of 10% EDTA in DI water to the scintillation vial containing the cochlea.
Circulate 2 mL of 10% EDTA in DI water through the cochlea using a transfer pipette.
Place the scintillation vial back on the rotator and rotate at 10 rpm for 72 h at room temperature.
Change the 10% EDTA solution every 24 h over a 72 h period.
Rinse the cochlea 3 times for 2 h each with 1x PBS to decalcify it.
Store the cochleae in a 10% anti-anti, 10% pen-strep solution in PBS at 4°C for up to 72 h.
Make a shallow incision with a scalpel lengthwise on each umbilical cord segment to unroll and expose the Wharton's jelly.
Remove blood vessels from the umbilical cord segments using forceps.
Wash umbilical cord segments twice in PBS.
Finely mince tissue segments with a scalpel.
Digest minced tissue in 50 mL of digestion medium (0.2% type 2 collagenase, 1% penicillin-streptomycin) in a Petri dish on an orbital shaker at 50 rpm overnight in a 5% CO2 incubator at 37 °C.
Dilute digestion medium at a ratio of 1:16 in 2% antibiotic-antimycotic in PBS the following day.
Centrifuge diluted cells at 500 x g for 10 min to pellet cells.
Discard supernatant and resuspend pellets in Mesenchymal Stem Cell Growth Medium (MSCGM).
Plate cells at a density of 7 x 10^3 cells/cm² in tissue culture treated T-75 flasks.
Culture HWJCs in MSCGM, expanding to passage 5 for experiments.
Wash stored cochleae in 1x PBS three times for 30 min each using aseptic technique.
Transfer cochleae into separate wells of a 24-well plate.
Add 1 mL of pre-warmed MSCGM to each well.
Incubate cochleae in a 5% CO2, 37 °C cell culture incubator for at least 1 hour before infusion of cells.
Dissociate hWJCs and resuspend them with 37 °C pre-warmed 1x PBS twice.
Add enough 37 °C pre-warmed Trypsin with 0.5% EDTA to cover the cell vessel surface.
Incubate hWJCs in a 5% CO2, 37 °C cell culture incubator for up to 5 minutes.
Verify that 90% of cells have detached by viewing under an inverted microscope.
Gently tap the sides of the flask if needed to dislodge attached cells.
Transfer hWJCs from the culture vessel to a 50-mL conical tube containing MSCGM equivalent to the volume of Trypsin used.
Centrifuge at 500 x g at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend hWJCs in MSCGM at a concentration of 500,000 cells/mL.
Transfer cochleae to a new 24-well plate using a transfer pipette.
Add a drop of MSCGM to each cochlea to prevent drying out.
Orient the cochlea with ultra-fine forceps so that the oval and round windows are facing up.
Draw up 0.2 mL resuspended hWJCs (100,000 cells) using a sterile 28.5-gauge insulin syringe with connected tubing.
Using sterilized fine forceps, position tubing over the oval window.
Perfuse the cochlea with 0.2 mL of resuspended hWJCs using a 28.5-gauge insulin syringe connected to polyethylene tubing over approximately 5 min.
Add 0.8 mL of 37 °C pre-warmed MSCGM to the well containing the cochlea to bring the total volume in the well to 1 mL.
Repeat steps for each cochlea using a fresh syringe and tubing each time.
Place perfused cochleae in a 5% CO2, 37°C cell culture incubator.
Change media three times per week.
Fix cochleae in 4% paraformaldehyde in 1x PBS overnight at 4 °C on a rocking platform.
Wash cochleae with 1x PBS three times for 5 min each.
Gradually dehydrate cochlea with ethanol and clear with an aliphatic hydrocarbon solvent before embedding in paraffin.
Section samples to a thickness of 10 µm using a microtome.
Mount samples on glass microscope slides.
